html:
Idris was the head of the Senussi order and the first and only king of Libya, from independence in December 1951 until he was overthrown in 1969.

The grandson of the order's founder, he led the Senussi through the wars with Italy, mostly from exile in Egypt. In the Second World War he sided with Britain. Afterwards the United Nations decided that Libya, until then three separate regions, should be one independent kingdom, and Idris became king in 1951.

Libya was one of the poorest countries in the world until oil was found in 1959. The king was old and distant, and corruption grew. While he was abroad in 1969, young officers led by Muammar Gaddafi took power. He died in exile in Cairo.
